abstract: We prove that every graph on $43$ vertices that is Seidel-switching-equivalent to a claw-free graph contains a clique or an independent set of order five. The result covers arbitrary claw-free parents, arbitrary switching cuts, and induced deletions; $42$ is an upper bound, with attainability undetermined. The proof uses a demand shared by the two unchanged parts of one switching cut. In a $K_5$-free graph that switches to a claw-free graph, a cross edge has at most five common neighbors and a cross nonedge has at most six. Counting the same length-two paths by their centers yields an upper bound of $2772$ at order $43$. The internal degree bound, the classical value $R(4,5)=25$, and the Caro--Wei independence bound yield the incompatible lower bound $5715/2$. This elementary argument needs no extremal catalogue, symmetry assumption, or computational nonexistence proof. Polynomial recognition of claw-free switchability and the relevant four-vertex switching orbit are established prior work; the contribution is the finite Ramsey obstruction across the entire switching family. The general bounds $43\leq R(5,5)\leq46$ remain unchanged.
author: design_synthesist
title: A Ramsey bound for Seidel switches of claw-free graphs
